scams.name: NAIA Airport Taxi Overcharge
scams.avoidance: Use Grab (rideshare app) from the designated Grab pickup zones at each terminal Or use the official airport taxi counters inside arrivals where rates are metered Never get in a taxi that won't run the meter — walk away
scams.location: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), all terminals

scams.name: New Friend Card Game
scams.avoidance: Never follow a stranger you just met to a private residence The 'friendly local with a connection to your home country' opener is the most common Manila scam intro If invited anywhere private within minutes of meeting someone, politely decline and leave
scams.location: Tourist areas near Intramuros and Ermita

scams.name: Kalesa Carriage Overcharge at Intramuros
scams.avoidance: Ask specifically: 'What is the TOTAL price for the full ride back to this point?' Official kalesa rates in Intramuros are posted — look for the tourism board rate card Pay only the pre-agreed amount — have exact change ready

scams.name: Money Changer Short Change
scams.avoidance: Count every bill yourself, in front of the teller, before leaving the counter Use ATMs or hotel exchange desks instead of street money changers Say clearly 'I need to count this' and do not be rushed
scams.location: Money changers in tourist districts and malls

scams.name: Fake Police Drug Setup
scams.avoidance: Never buy anything from street sellers in Manila's entertainment districts Real Philippine police do not collect cash fines on the street If approached, insist on going to the actual police station — scammers will back down
scams.location: Entertainment districts, particularly around Malate and Ermita

scams.name: Overpriced Jeepney 'Tourist' Fare
scams.avoidance: Carry exact change for jeepney fares — ask fellow passengers what the fare is before boarding The standard minimum fare is ₱13-15 for the first 4km Use Grab or the new EDSA Carousel BRT for hassle-free fixed-price travel
